content: Benzonatate is a medication prescribed to alleviate coughing caused by conditions such as the common cold, bronchitis, pneumonia, or other lung infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as antitussives, or cough suppressants. The medication works by suppressing the cough reflex in the lungs and airways. Benzonatate is available in two forms: liquid-filled capsules (also called perles) and regular capsules, both of which are taken orally. It is typically taken three times a day as needed. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. The capsules must be swallowed whole; do not suck or chew them, as this can release the medication in your mouth, potentially causing numbness and an increased risk of choking. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about alternative uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before taking benzonatate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to benzonatate, procaine (Novocain), tetracaine (Pontocaine), or any other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking benzonatate, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Be aware that benzonatate may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so it is advisable to avoid alcohol while taking it. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking benzonatate. If you are taking benzonatate as needed, you do not need to worry about missing a dose. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Benzonatate may cause side effects. Common, less severe side effects include upset stomach, constipation, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, nasal congestion, and a burning sensation in the eyes. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though rare, may include rash or hives, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, confusion, or hallucinations (seeing things that are not there). If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, consult your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store benzonatate in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include restlessness, uncontrollable shaking, seizures, or loss of consciousness. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
